ranked_root_causes_revised.cause: host-side terminator script killed pod during step-10000 save+push transaction. Specifically: trainer.save_model(checkpoint-10000) had started writing to local pod disk; the in-process HF Hub push thread had begun OR was about to begin transferring adapter_model.safetensors (~390MB) over the network; pod was destroyed before either local write fully flushed AND before HF git commit was published. The 5-second termination window is structurally incompatible with the 60-180s push duration observed on prior saves.

Training crashed at step ~10000 (post-trainer.train() but pre-trainer.save_model('final')) due to exception (OOM in final state dump, NaN in last-step gradient, HF token expiry, etc.); pid exited cleanly so terminator's ALIVE=0 detection was correct in declaring 'pid GONE without DONE'. In this slice the in-trainer step-10000 save also did not push due to the same 5-sec termination window racing the network push.

Pure HF push 401/network failure (token expiry mid-run, transient network blip during step-10000 push) WITHOUT terminator interference — local checkpoint-10000 dir would have written to pod disk fine but HF commit failed silently

raw10_caveats: (a) Terminator log captured the symptom (DONE=0 ALIVE=0 STEP=10000) but NOT the train.log tail past step-8008 — the pod-side scp was structurally guaranteed to fail because host_pod_terminator.sh.txt error-branch did not mkdir -p artifacts/ first (script bug already documented). So the 'training reached step 10000 cleanly vs crashed at step 9999' distinction is forever unresolvable in this run; it does not affect the step-10000 absence diagnosis but does mean cause-rank #1 vs #2 cannot be discriminated to better than the 0.85/0.10 split shown.

(b) HF API audit is comprehensive for what HF exposes — full commit chain back to initial commit, full tree at HEAD, refs (branches+tags) — but HF Hub does not expose deleted-commit history, git GC events, push attempts that 401'd, or any server-side telemetry on aborted uploads. The diagnosis 'step-10000 commit was never created' is provable; the diagnosis 'no push attempt was made' is inferred from HF API showing no rejected/orphan refs but cannot be proven (HF would not retain a record of a connection that died mid-upload before commit publish).

(c) Retroactive recovery is fully blocked. Pod 29dhlqk508ugoc was terminated via runpodctl pod delete which on RunPod is a hard-destroy (pod-state poll returns null per cost_analysis.json caveat b; ssh refused per this audit's pod_log_recovery_check). RunPod does not preserve container disk state after delete. There is no mechanism — paid or unpaid — to recover the step-10000 weights from this run.
